newsitem.title: USA: Electroglas cutting spending, orders soft.
newsitem.headline: Electroglas cutting spending, orders soft.

text.p: Electroglas Inc said on Thursday that it was reducing spending because the decline in capital equipment orders, which hurt its third quarter 1996 results, was expected to continue into 1997.

Chief Executive Officer Curt Wozniak said: "The continued turmoil in the semiconductor market during the third quarter has affected the near-term expansion plans of our customers. Many have delayed their capital equipment purchases between six months to a year. This has caused our orders to decline from the prior quarter."
Wozniak said the order delay hurt third quarter revenues and backlog, and the company expected the situation to continue into 1997.
Wozniak said Electroglas has already reduced its workforce by about 14 percent and curtailed discretionary spending.
The company, which makes automatic wafer probing equipment for the semiconductor industry, said revenues in the third quarter 1996 fell 31 percent from the same period a year ago to $31.5 million.
But Electroglas said it remained committed to product development and its Horizon 4090 product was in pilot production and was expected to be shipped in the fourth quarter.
